I will keep the whole 1.7 mu in maize, because my land is small, I know maize well, and after 50 years of farming I would rather manage one crop steadily than spread my effort. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on maize with a moderate-input plan: enough fertilizer to protect yield, but not so much that I waste money on a small plot. I will use hybrid seed because on a tiny area I care more about stable output than saving seed. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and fits the start of the season. I will irrigate a few key times, mainly around establishment and the heavier water-demand stages, because water control is one of the few things I can use to protect yield. I will also keep pesticide use limited and practical, applying only a small number of times as a normal seasonal protection plan. My goal is a steady maize harvest with manageable labor and input cost for my household.
